sections.body: Mental health is how we think, feel and cope. Everyone has mental health, just like physical health. It goes up and down.
Anxiety (worry), low mood and stress are common, especially during the teenage years. Signs to take seriously: feelings that last weeks, stop you doing normal things, or change sleep and appetite.
Things that help: sleep, exercise, time outdoors, talking to people you trust, limiting doom-scrolling, and being kind to yourself.
Getting help is a strength. Talk to a parent, teacher, school counsellor or doctor. If you ever feel unsafe, contact your local emergency number or a youth helpline straight away.

quiz.q: Which sign suggests it's time to talk to someone about how you feel?
options: Low mood that lasts weeks and stops you doing normal things
Being sad when your team loses
hints: Look for feelings that last a long time and affect daily life.
Being tired after one late night is normal. Being exhausted every day for weeks is worth checking.
quiz.explain: Feelings that last weeks and get in the way of daily life are a sign to reach out for help.

quiz.q: Which habit supports good mental health?
hints: Think about what helps your body and mind.
After a walk outside, people often feel calmer. Which option is like that?
quiz.explain: Regular sleep and exercise are proven to support mental health.
